newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/Swiss breakout a boon for dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/Swiss breakout a boon for dlr/mark.

text.p: A topside breakout on dollar/Swiss on Thursday fired up further an already bullish dollar/mark, leaving the door wide open for fresh highs on both trades, technical analysts said.

Dollar/Swiss first took out resistance at 1.4922, the prior 1997 high, raced through 1.5071, a level not seen since December 1993, and tested 1.51 -- its highest since November 1993's peak of 1.5125, now a key near-term resistance.
"Now that we have both dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss making new highs there's no reason for this not to go higher," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy.

Chase Securities technical analyst John Tirone said the dollar/Swiss rally was likely to be extended as the pair was firmly holding above the prior 1997 high. Tirone predicted a push to 1.52 and said even 1.54 was not out of the question.
"We're coming out of pretty big resistances and to me that's pretty significant," Tirone said.

CIBC's Autotte noted that dollar/Swiss, which earlier lagged dollar/mark, has now turned into a leader. He stressed there was no real resistance on the way to 1.8430, the cycle high in 1991. A break of that level would signal a rally to 1.8760, the target in an Elliott Wave analysis.
Autotte stressed the speed of the dollar/mark advance may be cause for a pause, although not necessarily a reason to rule out a straight extension of the rally.

"It seems to occur at the end of a move -- when euphoria gets into the market and it's easy to make money just by being long," Autotte said. "I'm not saying we're about to turnaround but you must be careful in these conditions."
Chase's Tirone said the dollar/mark rally should remain intact, provided that 1.8220 support holds. In late afternoon trading, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.8340/50, off from the day's high at 1.84.
If dollar/mark breaches 1.8430, the next high would take us back to November 1989, marked by a peak of 1.8690.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen remained mired in the 114.60-116.50 range. The pair, however, held close to the top of its range on Thursday, suggesting a breakout on the upside.
"We need to break either of the boundaries to get the momentum going again," said Autotte who noted dollar/yen repeatedly tested a double bottom at 115.55 on Thursday, only to bounce higher.
"I favor a break to the upside because usually these congestions are more like a pause in the market before it returns to its previous bullish trend," Autotte added.
